expectation: Cytoplasmic, granular signal around nuclei in macrophages and monocytes. Common in tumour stroma: scattered single cells and loose clusters at the tumour–stroma boundary, with some dense aggregates. A subset of these cells should also be CD163+ (M2-like).
observed: A: scattered yellow cells in every ROI, densest in stromal bands. One ROI has large confluent patches. B/C: a few elongated cytoplasmic cells among many negative nuclei. D: rings of cytoplasm around nuclei. E: CD68 cells sit largely on CD163 cells (white), with some CD68-only cells.
why: A distinct subset of cells shows cytoplasmic signal, is spread through the stroma, and overlaps strongly with CD163, as macrophages should.
notes: CD68 marks scattered and clustered cells with signal in the cytoplasm around the nucleus, and many of them are also CD163+. One ROI has large confluent yellow patches, which may be macrophage-rich areas or necrosis. They do not decide the verdict.
